subject: Pricing tiers and commitment options for high-volume hosted API
messages:
From: Avery Solutions <purchasing@averysolutions.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API rates for large-scale ingestion

Hi Connor,

Thanks for taking this. We're evaluating hosted providers for a new document-ingestion pipeline and have a pretty spiky but large token profile. High level: 50B tokens/month average, spikes to ~200B for short periods, retention of raw text for 30 days, and we need embeddings for search snapshots.

Two asks to start:
- Can you share your current hosted rate card and any volume discount thresholds?
- What pricing and SLA tradeoffs exist for customers at 50B+ and 200B+ tokens/month?

Our procurement window is tight (targeting an approved vendor list decision within 3 weeks). If it helps, I can share a sample usage CSV.

Thanks,
Avery (Purchasing)
Avery Solutions

--
Avery Solutions Procurement
procurement@averysolutions.com
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Avery Solutions <purchasing@averysolutions.com>, Samir Patel <samir@averysolutions.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API rates for large-scale ingestion

Hi Avery (and Samir),

Thanks — appreciate the context. Attached is our Q3 hosted rate card (Redwood_Hosted_RateCard_Q3_2026.pdf) and a short note on packaging. Quick summary up front:

- Baseline (pay-as-you-go): $0.0008 per token for generation; $0.0004 per token for embeddings.
- 12-month committed tiers (monthly committed tokens):
  • 50M–5B: baseline - 10%
  • 5B–50B: baseline - 18%
  • 50B–200B: baseline - 28%
  • 200B+: bespoke pricing (requires commitment or multi-region planning)

Those are starting points — we often structure deals with a blended rate based on expected distribution across generation vs embeddings and a commitment on monthly minimums. For SLA/credits, we can include latency SLOs tied to committed capacity (e.g., 95th %-ile latency target and credits for missed SLOs).

A few quick questions that will help me put together a precise proposal:
1) What percentage of tokens will be embeddings vs generation?
2) Do spikes to 200B occur regularly (e.g., seasonal) or are they short bursts?
3) Do you need region-specific hosting (US/EU) for data residency?

If you can share the sample CSV you mentioned (even an anonymized week), I can model blended pricing and a recommended commitment level. Happy to set up a call this week to walk through.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Connor — forwarding for visibility. Avery looks like a mid-enterprise deal; if they commit to a 12-month minimum we have discretionary room to move to a deeper discount for the 50B-200B band. Approve up to an additional 5% off the table you shared (so ~33% total for the 50B-200B band) provided:
- They commit to a 12-month term with monthly minimums at or above 100B tokens/month, and
- We include an SLA with defined latency SLOs and a 30-day pilot clause.

Laura — please prep a short contract appendix for SLO/credits and invoicing terms (net 45 typical for Avery?).

Ben

Connor — thanks for the quick reply. A few clarifications from engineering:
- Approximately 40% embedding tokens, 60% generation (mix of long-form and summarization).
- Spikes to ~200B are usually short (2–6 hours), occurring 2–4 times per month during batch runs. Baseline sustained is ~50B/month.
- We will start US-only; EU later in phase 2.

Procurement questions: what does a commitment of 100B/month look like for billing and overage handling? Also can you confirm whether pre-committed tokens can be banked within a quarter?

If you can provide a quick illustrative quote for two scenarios I can share internally:
A) 12-month term with 100B tokens/month commit (blended pricing, net 45 invoicing)
B) Pay-as-you-go with a 200B spike-handling add-on

I attached a sanitized sample usage (usage_sample.csv) to help modeling.

—Samir

Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API rates for large-scale ingestion

Samir — great, thanks for the details and the CSV. Modeling notes below (illustrative, final quote will be contractual):

Scenario A — 12-month commit, 100B tokens/month (US only)- Blended starting rate: $0.00068 per generation token; $0.00034 per embedding token (after existing 28% band discount + Ben's discretionary 5% = ~33% off baseline).
- Effective blended per-token: approx $0.00055 (weighted by 60/40 gen/embed).
- Bankability: up to 15% of monthly committed tokens can roll-forward within the quarter; overage billed at blended overage rate (10% premium over committed blended rate).
- SLA: 95th%-ile p50 latency targets included for committed capacity; credits up to 5% of monthly bill for sustained SLO miss.
- Invoicing: monthly in arrears, net 45; early-payment credit available on request.

Scenario B — Pay-as-you-go + spike handling- Baseline pay-as-you-go as previously stated; we offer a spike add-on (provisioned burst capacity) at a premium: 20% surcharge on tokens consumed during approved high-throughput windows.
- No bankability for pay-as-you-go; overages billed at standard rate.

Next steps I suggest:
1) If Scenario A looks reasonable I can produce a formal quote and draft MSA appendix (Laura will prepare SLO language).
2) If they prefer Scenario B, we can scope an initial 30-day pilot with burst capacity and review actual burst profiles to recommend a commit.

I'll attach the rate card again to this thread. Let me know which path Avery prefers and I'll pull a quote for your procurement packet.

Best,
Connor
